sections.h2: Where Huron County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Room 203 of the county building, 250 East Huron Avenue in Bad Axe (48413), is the recording desk. Phone 989-269-9941; fax 989-269-8786. The counter runs 8:30 to 4:30 on weekdays, holidays excepted, and nobody locks the door at noon.

The county's page for the office explains that the land record indexes are searchable online back to 1947, with older land records going back to 1848 kept in the office. Documents can be delivered by hand or mailed. Correct fees have to arrive with the paper, and payment can be a check, a money order, cash or a card.

sections.h2: Why older records get thin around 1865
sections.html:
A courthouse fire explains it. The Legislature created Huron County on April 1, 1840, and it was fully organized January 25, 1859. Sand Beach, today's Harbor Beach, hosted the county seat until the courthouse burned in 1865 and took most of the records with it. Government moved to Port Austin, and in 1873 the Board of Supervisors picked Bad Axe.

Farm and shoreline parcels held by one family for generations may therefore show gaps in the earliest paper. Ask the title company early how it plans to deal with the oldest links in the chain, and look through the paper books in Room 203 where the online index stops.

sections.h2: Checking the record before you list
sections.html:
Begin with the online index and write down the book and page, or the document number, of your own vesting deed. The county page also links to Laredo search details and to Property Fraud Alert enrollment. Laredo is the program title searchers use on the official record, and the alert tells an owner when a filed paper carries the exact name entered.

  • Pull the deed that put the property in your name, plus every mortgage, so you know what must be released at closing.
  • Scan the index for easements, land contracts and assignments touching the parcel.
  • Enroll your name as it appears on title, and add a second entry for any variant.
  • Call 989-269-9941 about anything older than 1947.

If a recorded paper surprises you, staff in Room 203 can help you find it in the index.

sections.h2: What a Huron County filing costs
sections.html:
Michigan sets a $30.00 charge for each recorded document, however many pages it has, in MCL 600.2567. The smaller items below may also appear on a seller's bill.

Huron County recording charges
ServiceCharge
Record one document$30.00
Each added instrument reached by one assignment or discharge$3.00
Certify a document on record$5.00
Photocopy$1.00 per page
Grantor or grantee search50 cents per year, $5.00 minimum

The charge is due as the paper is left for recording; for an electronic filing the statute gives one business day. Huron County names two e-recording firms: Simplifile, 1-800-460-5657, and CSC, 1-866-652-0111. For an unusual instrument, call the register to learn the exact amount.

Two levies run on the price: $3.75 for each $500 or part of $500 as the state's share in MCL 207.525, and 55 cents per $500 as the county's share in MCL 207.504, which applies to a county under 2,000,000 residents. Divide the price by $500, round up, and multiply by the combined rate. The instrument must state the whole value, or an affidavit of value is attached.

The two acts diverge on family deeds. The state list in MCL 207.526 excuses a conveyance to a child or grandchild, yet the county list in MCL 207.505 has no such line. Ask the register before a parent signs a house over to a son or daughter.

sections.h2: What trips up a deed headed for Bad Axe
sections.html:
The recording statute, MCL 565.201, lists what a register of deeds may insist on. Walk through it with the drafter:

  • The typed name under every signature should match the name the notary wrote in the acknowledgment.
  • The notary's printed or stamped name belongs on the same page, near the notary signature.
  • A deed signed after January 1, 1964 carries its drafter's name and business address.
  • Cover or remove the first five digits of any Social Security number.
  • Attach a written English translation to any paper in another language.

When a paper is accepted and recorded, the statute treats it as conforming, and a compliant instrument cannot be refused for what it says.

sections.h2: Selling in the Thumb's northern tip
sections.html: Huron County has Saginaw Bay on the west and Lake Huron on the north and east, with over 90 miles of shoreline. Farming leads the economy, and weekend visitors concentrate around Port Austin and Caseville. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $154,300, and owners occupy 81.8 percent of homes. The county's home page links an Assessing and Tax Search tool and a FetchGIS map, both handy for checking acreage and the parcel number before a deed is drafted.

sections.h2: Other offices in the Huron County building
sections.html: The Treasurer's Office is in Room 204 of that building at 989-269-9238, open 8:30 to 4:30 with no lunch closure. Equalization is in Room 306 at 989-269-6497, sharing the room with Tax Mapping and GIS at 989-269-9421. Ask the Treasurer about the parcel's tax standing before the closing date so any balance is cleared out of the proceeds. The Huron County Land Bank operates from that same Treasurer's office. If the owner has died and the house passes through an estate, Probate Court is in Room 206 at 989-269-9944, and the County Clerk is in Room 201 at 989-269-9942.

Your title company or attorney will usually handle this, but it helps to know the sequence. The signed and notarized deed is checked against the list above, then sent by e-recording or delivered to Room 203. The fee and transfer tax are paid with it. Once the office records the deed, it becomes part of the public index, and the Treasurer and assessing units update their files from it. Ask for the recording information afterward and keep it with your closing papers. If a mistake turns up later, such as a misspelled name, a corrective instrument is recorded as a new document at its own $30.00 charge, so it pays to read the deed carefully before it is signed. A seller who has a mortgage should also confirm that the lender's release was recorded, since a lingering lien can surface when the buyer's title company searches the index.

faqs.q: When can I reach the Huron County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except holidays, with no break at noon. The office is Room 203 at 250 East Huron Avenue, Bad Axe.

faqs.q: Can a Huron County deed be e-recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile and CSC are the listed e-recording providers, so contact one of them and the office receives the document electronically.

faqs.q: How far back can I search Huron County deeds?
faqs.a: Online indexes begin in 1947, and land records from 1848 forward are held in the office. The 1865 courthouse fire at Sand Beach destroyed most early records.

faqs.q: Does a gift deed to my daughter owe transfer tax in Huron County?
faqs.a: The state tax exempts conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, while the county act's list shows no matching item. Call 989-269-9941 before counting on it, and state the exemption on the deed.

faqs.q: How do I pay the Huron County register of deeds?
faqs.a: Use a check, money order, cash or credit card, and include the correct fees with each recording. Checks may be made out straight to the Register of Deeds.
